function: RL agent allocates the 106 uplink resource blocks among NTN, guard band and TN (guard-band size and position) to maximize SINR and coverage probability (pp. 8-9).
system: LEO satellite at 600 km, 19 beams; 37 three-sector TN gNBs, 10 UEs per cell and beam; S-band 2 GHz, 20 MHz; no RIS (pp. 5, 11).
method: Double DQN, two 128-unit fully connected layers, 3 inputs, 7 actions; reinforcement learning with replay memory, with a stochastic-geometry interference approximation (pp. 2, 10).
data_channel: Own simulator on 3GPP models: TN urban-macro LoS path loss (TR 38.901); NTN basic path loss, shadowing, clutter (TR 38.811); no small-scale fading (pp. 4-5).
test_conditions: No separate training and testing conditions stated; setup of 10 UEs per beam and cell (p. 11); sweeps of 0-20 UEs with density-selected agents (pp. 11, 14).
baselines: Non-learned: fixed allocation, distributed greedy algorithm (DGA), joint bandwidth-partition and power-control optimization (JOBP); an undefined 'enhanced solution'; no learned baseline (p. 14).
metrics: SINR (average and CDF), coverage probability, reward convergence, computational complexity (pp. 11-15).
complexity: Training O(E*T*B*C), C = multiplications per forward pass (Eq. 36); inference one forward pass O(C); Table V compares DGA, JOBP, RA-DDQN (pp. 10, 15).
openness: none; simulations implemented in Python, no code or data link (p. 11).
q1_support: p. 4: "The NTN model follows the 3GPP specifications [44]." and "The TN is modeled on the basis of 3GPP specifications as defined in [47]"; p. 5: "modeled based on the basic path-loss model [49]". Refs [47] = TR 38.901 (p. 16) and [49] = TR 38.811 (p. 17); only large-scale loss, no fading.
q2_support: p. 11: "it dynamically selects an appropriate agent that has been trained for similar network conditions". Not met: no model is tested outside its training conditions; the sweeps over 0-20 UEs (p. 14) use density-matched agents and Table III (p. 11) gives one setup.
q3_support: p. 14: "three conventional resource allocation strategies: 1) fixed allocation; 2) distributed greedy algorithm (DGA); and 3) the joint optimization of bandwidth partition and power control (JOBP)". Not met: only non-learned baselines; no earlier learned method is compared, and the "enhanced solution" is never defined.
q4_support: p. 10: "Therefore, the total time complexity over training is O(E · T · B · C)"; p. 15: "requires only a single forward pass O(C) during inference".
q5_support: p. 11: "The simulations were implemented in Python". Not met: no code or data link or DOI anywhere; the channel comes from the authors' own simulator, not a public dataset.
notes: Included as area 6: the RL agent controls the bandwidth blocks and guard band of a LEO satellite uplink that shares spectrum with a terrestrial network, which is resource control of a satellite link (pp. 8-9). Channel has only large-scale terms; reference [47] is printed as 38.9091 but is titled as the TR 38.901 channel model (p. 16). The 'enhanced solution' of Figs. 15-16 is never defined, so it is not counted as a learned baseline. q1 is a judgement: the paper says its models follow 3GPP, reviewer to confirm that large-scale-only use counts.
